sentences.text: A lower rate cuts the monthly payment.
sentences.spoken: A lower rate cuts the monthly payment.

sentences.text: But the refinance has a price, and the savings must repay it first.
sentences.spoken: But the refinance has a price... and the savings must repay it first.

sentences.text: So how far do rates have to fall before a refinance pays for itself?
sentences.spoken: So how far do rates have to fall... before a refinance pays for itself?

sentences.text: This is a lab for money decisions: we run the numbers on public data and show every assumption.
sentences.spoken: This is a lab for money decisions... we run the numbers on public data and show every assumption.

sentences.text: US only. The rates here are history, not a forecast.
sentences.spoken: U.S. only. The rates here are history... not a forecast.

sentences.text: By the end, you will see the exact rate drop that repays a typical refinance within 36 months, and how every rate drop since 1971 actually played out.
sentences.spoken: By the end... you will see the exact rate drop that repays a typical refinance within thirty-six months... and how every rate drop since nineteen seventy-one actually played out.

sentences.text: Here is the rate itself: the weekly average for a 30-year fixed mortgage, from Freddie Mac's survey.
sentences.spoken: Here is the rate itself... the weekly average for a thirty-year fixed mortgage... from Freddie Mac's survey.

sentences.text: It peaked at 18.63% in 1981.
sentences.spoken: It peaked at eighteen point six three percent... in nineteen eighty-one.

sentences.text: It bottomed at 2.65% in 2021.
sentences.spoken: It bottomed at two point six five percent... in twenty twenty-one.

sentences.text: Every fall in that line is a moment when homeowners asked the same question.
sentences.spoken: Every fall in that line is a moment... when homeowners asked the same question.

sentences.text: First question, then: what does a refinance actually cost?
sentences.spoken: First question... then... what does a refinance actually cost?

sentences.text: Lenders report it for every loan they make, under the Home Mortgage Disclosure Act, as total loan costs.
sentences.spoken: Lenders report it for every loan they make... under the Home Mortgage Disclosure Act... as total loan costs.

sentences.text: Those are the closing costs: origination charges, discount points, the appraisal, title insurance, and the rest.
sentences.spoken: Those are the closing costs... origination charges... discount points... the appraisal... title insurance... and the rest.

sentences.text: Discount points are optional: paying more at closing buys a lower rate, so part of that bill is a choice.
sentences.spoken: Discount points are optional... paying more at closing buys a lower rate... so part of that bill is a choice.

sentences.text: Cash-out refinances, which also take equity out of the house, cost more: a median of $8,655. This film keeps to refinances that change only the rate and the term.
sentences.spoken: Cash-out refinances... which also take equity out of the house... cost more... a median of eight thousand six hundred fifty-five dollars. This film keeps to refinances that change only the rate and the term.

sentences.text: In 2025, lenders reported 488,241 of those, into 30-year first mortgages.
sentences.spoken: In twenty twenty-five... lenders reported four hundred eighty-eight thousand two hundred forty-one of those... into thirty-year first mortgages.

sentences.text: In nominal dollars, the median one cost $5,124.
sentences.spoken: In nominal dollars... the median one cost five thousand one hundred twenty-four dollars.

sentences.text: The middle half paid between $3,443 and $8,270.
sentences.spoken: The middle half paid between three thousand four hundred forty-three dollars... and eight thousand two hundred seventy dollars.

sentences.text: The count follows the rate. In 2021, near the bottom, lenders reported 3,089,298 of them.
sentences.spoken: The count follows the rate. In twenty twenty-one... near the bottom... lenders reported three million eighty-nine thousand two hundred ninety-eight of them.

sentences.text: Their median bill that year was $3,406.
sentences.spoken: Their median bill that year was three thousand four hundred six dollars.

sentences.text: But the dollar figure hides the real pattern. The bill barely grows with the size of the loan.
sentences.spoken: But the dollar figure hides the real pattern. The bill barely grows... with the size of the loan.

sentences.text: On loans under $150,000, the median cost was 3.4% of the amount borrowed.
sentences.spoken: On loans under one hundred fifty thousand dollars... the median cost was three point four percent of the amount borrowed.

sentences.text: On loans of $750,000 and more, it was 0.5%.
sentences.spoken: On loans of seven hundred fifty thousand dollars and more... it was zero point five percent.

sentences.text: So the same cut in rate repays a large loan faster than a small one. Keep that in mind; it comes back.
sentences.spoken: So the same cut in rate repays a large loan faster than a small one. Keep that in mind... it comes back.

sentences.text: Paying the bill back is simple division: the closing costs, divided by the drop in the monthly payment.
sentences.spoken: Paying the bill back is simple division... the closing costs... divided by the drop in the monthly payment.

sentences.text: The answer is the break-even: the month when the savings have covered the bill.
sentences.spoken: The answer is the break-even... the month when the savings have covered the bill.

sentences.text: Before that month, the refinance is still in the red. After it, every payment is money kept.
sentences.spoken: Before that month... the refinance is still in the red. After it... every payment is money kept.

sentences.text: Now the main question: how big does the drop have to be?
sentences.spoken: Now the main question... how big does the drop have to be?

sentences.text: Take the median refinance: a balance of $375,000, and $5,124 to close.
sentences.spoken: Take the median refinance... a balance of three hundred seventy-five thousand dollars... and five thousand one hundred twenty-four dollars to close.

sentences.text: Say the old loan carries 7.62%, the average rate in the month the last big drop began, October 2023.
sentences.spoken: Say the old loan carries seven point six two percent... the average rate in the month the last big drop began... October twenty twenty-three.

sentences.text: Cut the rate by 0.25 points, and the payment falls by $64 a month.
sentences.spoken: Cut the rate by zero point two five points... and the payment falls by sixty-four dollars a month.

sentences.text: At that pace, the bill takes 80 months to come back.
sentences.spoken: At that pace... the bill takes eighty months to come back.

sentences.text: Double the cut to 0.5 points, and the payment falls by $128 a month.
sentences.spoken: Double the cut to zero point five points... and the payment falls by one hundred twenty-eight dollars a month.

sentences.text: Break-even arrives in 41 months.
sentences.spoken: Break-even arrives in forty-one months.

sentences.text: A cut of 1 point saves $253 a month.
sentences.spoken: A cut of one point saves two hundred fifty-three dollars a month.

sentences.text: That pays back the bill in 21 months.
sentences.spoken: That pays back the bill in twenty-one months.

sentences.text: 2 points pay back in 11 months, well inside a year.
sentences.spoken: two points pay back in eleven months... well inside a year.

sentences.text: Look at the shape of that curve. It is not a straight line.
sentences.spoken: Look at the shape of that curve. It is not a straight line.

sentences.text: Below 0.5 points it climbs steeply: each smaller cut adds years, not months.
sentences.spoken: Below zero point five points it climbs steeply... each smaller cut adds years... not months.

sentences.text: That is where the common rule of thumb about a full point comes from: for this loan, 1 point pays back in 21 months, 0.5 points in 41.
sentences.spoken: That is where the common rule of thumb about a full point comes from... for this loan... one point pays back in twenty-one months... zero point five points in forty-one.

sentences.text: But remember the pattern in the costs, and move the same question to a different loan.
sentences.spoken: But remember the pattern in the costs... and move the same question to a different loan.

sentences.text: To break even within 36 months, the median loan needs a cut of 0.56 points.
sentences.spoken: To break even within thirty-six months... the median loan needs a cut of zero point five six points.

sentences.text: A loan under $150,000 needs 1.32 points, because its bill is a bigger share of the balance.
sentences.spoken: A loan under one hundred fifty thousand dollars needs one point three two points... because its bill is a bigger share of the balance.

sentences.text: A loan of $750,000 or more needs only 0.2.
sentences.spoken: A loan of seven hundred fifty thousand dollars or more needs only zero point two.

sentences.text: Give the median loan 60 months instead, and 0.33 points is enough.
sentences.spoken: Give the median loan sixty months instead... and zero point three three points is enough.

sentences.text: Give it 84 months, and it needs 0.24.
sentences.spoken: Give it eighty-four months... and it needs zero point two four.

sentences.text: Read each of those as a flip point: below it, the bill outlasts the stay; above it, the savings win.
sentences.spoken: Read each of those as a flip point... below it... the bill outlasts the stay... above it... the savings win.

sentences.text: So there is no single threshold. The drop that pays back depends on two things: how big the loan is, and how long it is kept.
sentences.spoken: So there is no single threshold. The drop that pays back depends on two things... how big the loan is... and how long it is kept.

sentences.text: And how long it is kept is the one number no dataset can supply.
sentences.spoken: And how long it is kept is the one number no dataset can supply.

sentences.text: One more cost hides inside the new loan. It starts a fresh 30 years, so the last payment moves further away, even when each payment is smaller.
sentences.spoken: One more cost hides inside the new loan. It starts a fresh thirty years... so the last payment moves further away... even when each payment is smaller.

sentences.text: The simple division ignores that. It answers only the first question: when do the savings cover the bill?
sentences.spoken: The simple division ignores that. It answers only the first question... when do the savings cover the bill?

sentences.text: The division assumes the new rate is the last one. What happened in the real drops?
sentences.spoken: The division assumes the new rate is the last one. What happened... in the real drops?

sentences.text: We found every fall of at least 1 point in the 30-year rate since 1971: 13 of them.
sentences.spoken: We found every fall of at least one point in the thirty-year rate since nineteen seventy-one... thirteen of them.

sentences.text: In each, a borrower who took a loan at the peak refinances in the first month the rate is 1 point lower.
sentences.spoken: In each... a borrower who took a loan at the peak refinances in the first month the rate is one point lower.

sentences.text: Closing costs use the median share for that year; before 2018, lenders did not report them, so a fixed share is used and marked illustrative.
sentences.spoken: Closing costs use the median share for that year... before twenty eighteen... lenders did not report them... so a fixed share is used and marked illustrative.

sentences.text: The steepest falls came in the early 1980s.
sentences.spoken: The steepest falls came in the early nineteen-eighties.

sentences.text: After the peak of 1981, the first cut of 1 point came 2 months later.
sentences.spoken: After the peak of nineteen eighty-one... the first cut of one point came two months later.

sentences.text: It paid back in 13 months, but the slide went on, and the next point came 9 months after the refinance.
sentences.spoken: It paid back in thirteen months... but the slide went on... and the next point came nine months after the refinance.

sentences.text: Some drops were brief. The fall that began in 1987 lasted 4 months, and the refinance came at its very bottom.
sentences.spoken: Some drops were brief. The fall that began in nineteen eighty-seven lasted four months... and the refinance came at its very bottom.

sentences.text: The drop that began in 2006 was slower. The refinance came in January 2008, and it had paid for itself before the next point arrived.
sentences.spoken: The drop that began in two thousand six was slower. The refinance came in January two thousand eight... and it had paid for itself before the next point arrived.

sentences.text: At a cut of 1 point, break-even took between 10 and 21 months across all 13 drops.
sentences.spoken: At a cut of one point... break-even took between ten and twenty-one months across all thirteen drops.

sentences.text: But in 5 of them, the rate kept falling: another drop of 1 point before the first refinance had paid for itself.
sentences.spoken: But in five of them... the rate kept falling... another drop of one point before the first refinance had paid for itself.

sentences.text: Those borrowers met the same question twice, and a second refinance starts a new clock with a new bill.
sentences.spoken: Those borrowers met the same question twice... and a second refinance starts a new clock with a new bill.

sentences.text: In the drop that began in November 2018, the refinance came in June 2019.
sentences.spoken: In the drop that began in November twenty eighteen... the refinance came in June twenty nineteen.

sentences.text: It needed 18 months to break even, and the next drop of 1 point came only 17 months later.
sentences.spoken: It needed eighteen months to break even... and the next drop of one point came only seventeen months later.

sentences.text: In the other 8, the first refinance was the one that mattered.
sentences.spoken: In the other eight... the first refinance was the one that mattered.

sentences.text: The latest drop began in October 2023. The cut of 1 point arrived in August 2024.
sentences.spoken: The latest drop began... in October twenty twenty-three. The cut of one point arrived in August twenty twenty-four.

sentences.text: At that year's median cost, it paid back in 21 months.
sentences.spoken: At that year's median cost... it paid back in twenty-one months.

sentences.text: So, how far do rates have to fall before a refinance pays for itself?
sentences.spoken: So... how far do rates have to fall before a refinance pays for itself?

sentences.text: For the median loan and median costs, a cut that repays it within 36 months is 0.56 points.
sentences.spoken: For the median loan and median costs... a cut that repays it within thirty-six months is zero point five six points.

sentences.text: Half as much patience asks for more: to pay back in 21 months takes 1 point.
sentences.spoken: Half as much patience asks for more... to pay back in twenty-one months takes one point.

sentences.text: That answer has limits. It counts payment savings only: no taxes, no return on the cash, and a new 30-year loan restarts the clock on owning the house outright.
sentences.spoken: That answer has limits. It counts payment savings only... no taxes... no return on the cash... and a new thirty-year loan restarts the clock on owning the house outright.

sentences.text: It uses medians: half of borrowers paid more than $5,124, and an offered rate can differ from the survey average.
sentences.spoken: It uses medians... half of borrowers paid more than five thousand one hundred twenty-four dollars... and an offered rate can differ from the survey average.

sentences.text: And it is history, not a forecast: nothing here says where rates go next.
sentences.spoken: And it is history... not a forecast... nothing here says where rates go next.

sentences.text: What history does show is the shape of the trade: a known bill up front, against savings that arrive one month at a time, for as long as the loan lasts.
sentences.spoken: What history does show is the shape of the trade... a known bill up front... against savings that arrive one month at a time... for as long as the loan lasts.

sentences.text: Method. Rates are Freddie Mac's weekly survey via FRED, checked against the Optimal Blue index since 2017.
sentences.spoken: Method. Rates are Freddie Mac's weekly survey via Fred... checked against the Optimal Blue index since twenty seventeen.

sentences.text: A drop counts when the monthly average falls at least 1 point from a peak before rising 1 point from its low.
sentences.spoken: A drop counts when the monthly average falls at least one point... from a peak before rising one point from its low.

sentences.text: Costs are HMDA loan-level data from 2018 to 2025: originated refinances, first lien, 30-year term.
sentences.spoken: Costs are H.M.D.A. loan-level data from twenty eighteen to twenty twenty-five... originated refinances... first lien... thirty-year term.

sentences.text: Closing costs are paid in cash, with no taxes and no discounting. Every figure and formula is listed in the description.
sentences.spoken: Closing costs are paid in cash... with no taxes and no discounting. Every figure and formula is listed in the description.

sentences.text: A small cut needs a long stay. A large loan needs a smaller cut. And a falling rate can make the first refinance too early.
sentences.spoken: A small cut needs a long stay. A large loan needs a smaller cut.... And a falling rate can make the first refinance too early.

sentences.text: The break-even is simple division. The hard part is the number only the borrower knows: how long the loan will be kept.
sentences.spoken: The break-even is simple division. The hard part is the number only the borrower knows... how long the loan will be kept.

sentences.text: The bill is known the day the loan closes. The savings arrive one month at a time.
sentences.spoken: The bill is known the day the loan closes. The savings arrive one month at a time.

sentences.text: The sources are linked in the description, and the next decision is already on the bench.
sentences.spoken: The sources are linked in the description... and the next decision is already on the bench.
